text:
support_jen: Heads up — multiple customers reporting 503s and timeouts starting ~09:12 PT. High % of failures for hosted/text-generation routes. Affected customers: @acme, @bixly. Error surface looks like upstream inference worker exits followed by gateway 503s. :rotating_light:

jordan: Do we have an initial s3 of logs or stack traces? any recent deploys?

samir: I pulled one of the runner logs from host-34: shows a segfault immediately after a CUDA OOM-ish spike. snippet: 
```
[2026-03-15T16:12:34Z] INFO runtime: starting batch size=48 seq_len=4096 model=redwood-v0.6
[2026-03-15T16:12:34Z] WARN kv_prefetch: mem_high_water=0.92
[2026-03-15T16:12:35Z] ERROR infer: worker: signal 11 (Segmentation fault)
*** End of stack trace ***
```

alice: That stack trace looks like the process died not graceful OOM. I also grabbed the host's dmesg: kernel reported GPU page fault + context loss.

deploy-bot: Deployment 5529873000: rolled quant-profile "aggressive-fp4" to us-west-2 at 09:05 PT (author: samir).

jordan: @samir you rolled the quant-profile yesterday? Could that interact with the new batching heuristics we rolled this morning?

samir: Yes — the `aggressive-fp4` profile reduces memory per shard but changes kernel codepath. We also adjusted autoscaler target throughput at 08:58 PT increasing max batch size from 32->64. Possible combined effect.

support_jen: Customer impact: several requests retried by SDK and got 503s; a few customers reported billing anomalies because their retries consumed quota. CS already opened cases.

alice: Quick repro attempt: run a request with long context + concurrent QPS to force large batch. curl example: 
```bash
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate 
 -H 'Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN' 
 -d '{"model":"redwood-v0.6","max_tokens":1500,"prompt":"<long prompt>"}'
```
With 40 parallel workers I can reproduce a crash within ~2-3 minutes against a dev pool.

opsbot: Observability alert: evictions on gpu-node-34 spiked at 09:11-09:15 PT. 6 runner exits in 4m.

sre-oncall: Escalating to SRE runtime team. Triage steps: (1) pin traffic off affected hosts, (2) revert the autoscaler batch-size bump to 32, (3) roll back quant-profile to previous stable.

samir: I can revert quant-profile to `stable-v3` immediately if SRE approves. Also will create a minimal repro script & collect core dump.

jordan: Thanks. @sre-oncall please confirm when hosts are cordoned so we can update customers. Also need a postmortem checklist: collect core dumps, nvidia-smi logs, and full runner logs for the 2m prior to crash.

alice: Added quick repro steps in #devex-repro with runbook and the small harness that ramps batch size and concurrency. Link: https://goto/repro/5529873210

support_jen: CS update: told customers we are investigating, asked them to keep retry behavior conservative. Sending immediate credits for request retries.

sre-oncall: Action items assigned: samir -> rollback quant-profile (in 5m), infra -> revert autoscaler batch cap (in 10m), alice -> collect flame/kv-metrics and repro artifacts, jordan -> coordinate customer comms. Will update here when rollback complete.

samir: rollback started at 09:22 PT. I hit a small snag on one pool (auth token rotation), fixing now.

deploy-bot: Rollback 5529873211: quant-profile -> stable-v3 applied to us-west-2.

opsbot: Hosts cordoned: gpu-node-34,gpu-node-35. Traffic rerouted.

sre-oncall: Observability: runner exits dropped to zero after rollback and autoscaler revert. Gateways report 503s returning to normal within 3m of step completion.

support_jen: Customer follow-up: some still see elevated latency for a short window but no new 503s. CS will keep open cases until tomorrow.

jordan: Postmortem notes starter: probable root cause = interaction between aggressive quantization kernel path + sudden larger batch sizes causing GPU page faults and segfaults. Next: add crash guard in runtime for kernel fallbacks, tighten canary for quant-profile, and add autoscaler safety cap when host GPU health degraded.

alice: I'll attach the core dump, nvidia-smi timelines, and repro harness in the ticket. Also recommend a short-term mitigation: disable aggressive-fp4 in prod until 2-week canary passes.

support_jen: Thanks team. Will draft customer-facing summary for tomorrow. :thumbsup:
